answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents mint a unique identity token through zero-knowledge proofs verifying cryptographic attestation chains from past work. Registration requires staking bonded collateral governed by a velvet contract where validation fees scale superlinearly as $O(k^{1.5})$. A lightweight sparrow agent verifies execution proofs cheaply, but a malicious swarm faces exponential capital exhaustion. This design protects the pearl of decentralized consensus from forged identities.
